item.text:
I completed a targeted continuation pass. The repository and attempt directory could not be read or written because the sandbox failed with `RTM_NEWADDR`; therefore I could not persist `research-materials.md` or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The manifest changes are specified below for the parent to apply.

## New or repaired evidence units

### E-143 — CTBT ratification, with precise locator

- Claim: Türkiye deposited its CTBT ratification instrument with the UN Secretary-General on 16 February 2000 and contributed a seismic-monitoring station.
- Source: CTBTO press release.
- Locator: page lines 222–228.
- Period fit: direct 2000 act.
- Attribution: Turkish state action during Ecevit’s premiership; no direct personal signature or cabinet record located.
- Contrary/limit: state-level attribution cannot establish Ecevit’s personal responsibility.
- Links: 1B.4, 1B.10.
- Source: [CTBTO press release](https://www.ctbto.org/resources/for-the-media/press-releases/turkiye-ratifies-comprehensive-nuclear-test-ban-treaty)

### E-144 — IAEA Additional Protocol signature, with precise treaty locator

- Claim: The IAEA Board approved the Additional Protocol on 7 June 2000; Türkiye signed it on 6 July 2000; it entered into force on 17 July 2001.
- Source: IAEA INFCIRC/295/Add.1.
- Locator: paragraph 1, PDF p. 1.
- Period fit: signing is within 2000; entry into force is post-period.
- Attribution: Turkish state-level nonproliferation act; no direct Ecevit signature or cabinet record located.
- Contrary/limit: the protocol was not legally in force during the target year.
- Links: 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.10.
- Source: [IAEA INFCIRC/295/Add.1](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/publications/documents/infcircs/1982/infcirc295a1.pdf)

### E-151 — Nuclear Suppliers Group membership

- Claim: Türkiye’s NSG membership was endorsed on 20 April 2000; required procedures were completed in May, and a Turkish MFA/Atomic Energy Authority delegation attended NSG meetings in Paris on 19–23 June 2000.
- Source: Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 26 June 2000.
- Locator: press-release body, paragraphs beginning “Turkey’s membership…” and “Following the completion…”.
- Period fit: direct 2000 institutional act.
- Attribution: government/institutional attribution; no direct Ecevit decision record.
- Contrary/limit: NSG membership is a nonproliferation regime act, not evidence of nuclear command authority or weapons policy.
- Links: 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.10.
- Source: [Turkish MFA NSG statement](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/the-turkey_s-membership-to-the-nuclear-suppliers-group_unoffical-translation__br_no_114--_june-26_-2000.en.mfa)

### E-152 — U.S.–Türkiye peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement

- Claim: Türkiye and the United States signed a peaceful nuclear-energy cooperation agreement in Ankara on 26 July 2000. The agreement incorporated IAEA safeguards and peaceful-use controls; it entered into force only in 2008.
- Source: Turkish MFA retrospective.
- Locator: paragraphs 36–41.
- Period fit: signature within 2000; legal entry into force is post-period.
- Attribution: bilateral government act during Ecevit’s premiership; personal attribution not established.
- Contrary/limit: the agreement concerns peaceful nuclear cooperation, not nuclear weapons or NATO nuclear-sharing command.
- Links: 1B.7, 1B.10.
- Source: [Turkish MFA statement](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/no-98---3-june-2008_--press-release-regarding-the-the-agreement-for-cooperation-between-the-united-states-of-america-and-the-republic-of-turkey-concerning-the-peaceful-uses-of-nuclear-energy.en.mfa)

### E-153 — March 2000 fiscal, banking, and social-security implementation

- Claim: The March 10 government letter reports parliamentary approval of the 2000 budget, a discretionary-spending cut, disclosure of contingent liabilities, takeover of five commercial banks by SDIF, closure of one investment bank, planned social-security administration legislation, and Bag-Kur cost-control measures.
- Source: IMF Letter of Intent.
- Locator: paragraphs 3, 9–12; lines 38–60.
- Period fit: implementation evidence within early 2000, while some reported results concern late 1999.
- Attribution: collective Turkish government program, signed by State Minister Recep Önal and Central Bank Governor Gazi Erçel; no personal Ecevit signature.
- Contrary/limit: the same document records mixed real-economy conditions and continuing inflation risks.
- Links: 5B.3, 5B.6, 6B.2, 6B.9, 8B.2, 8B.6.
- Source: [IMF March 10, 2000 letter](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/01/index.htm)

### E-154 — June 2000 fiscal and distributional measures

- Claim: The June 22 letter records Bag-Kur health-cost controls, increased health premiums and co-payments, pension-system legislation, expenditure ceilings excluding earthquake-related expenses, salary adjustments, and minimum social-security contribution changes.
- Source: IMF Letter of Intent.
- Locator: paragraphs 7–10 and 13; lines 43–63.
- Period fit: direct mid-2000 policy implementation.
- Attribution: collective government policy; personal Ecevit responsibility is not established.
- Contrary/limit: the measures included cost containment and increased premiums/co-payments, creating distributional tradeoffs.
- Links: 5B.3, 5B.8, 6B.2, 6B.6, 6B.7, 8B.2.
- Source: [IMF June 22, 2000 letter](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/02/index.htm)

### E-155 — December 2000 program results and shortfalls

- Claim: The December 18 letter reports inflation projected at approximately 38% rather than the 25% target, primary-surplus performance above target, projected 2000 privatization receipts of $3.5 billion versus the $7.5 billion target, and expected real GNP growth above the 5–5.5% target range.
- Source: IMF Letter of Intent.
- Locator: paragraphs 2–5; lines 32–41.
- Period fit: direct end-2000 assessment.
- Attribution: government-reported program performance; not evidence of Ecevit’s individual competence.
- Contrary/limit: the same record documents a major inflation-target miss and privatization shortfall.
- Links: 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10, 8B.7, 8B.8.
- Source: [IMF December 18, 2000 letter](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/03/index.htm)

### E-156 — 2000 anti-corruption investigations and coalition responsibility

- Claim: A December 5, 2000 CSIS Turkey update reports public investigations into Egebank, Etibank, and other collapsed banks; it separately describes Ecevit’s “indulgence” toward Yılmaz in cabinet allocation and states that corruption continued under the coalition despite reputations for personal honesty.
- Source: CSIS Turkey Project report.
- Locator: PDF pp. 2–3, lines 80–112 and 115–128.
- Period fit: direct December 2000 reporting.
- Attribution: evidence about coalition composition and contemporary external assessment, not a finding that Ecevit personally benefited from corruption.
- Contrary/limit: the report itself distinguishes Ecevit’s reputation for honesty from the coalition’s institutional corruption problem; its language is analytical rather than adjudicative.
- Links: 7B.5, 7B.6, 7B.9, 8B.5.
- Source: [CSIS Turkey Update, 5 December 2000](https://csis-website-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/legacy_files/files/media/csis/pubs/tu001205.pdf)

### E-157 — TCIP official institutional description

- Claim: The Turkish Catastrophe Insurance Pool was established in 2000 as a public institution responsible for compulsory earthquake insurance, implementation, administration, rapid compensation, and broad low-premium access.
- Source: Turkish Catastrophe Insurance Pool/DASK.
- Locator: page lines 256–269.
- Period fit: establishment is explicitly dated to 2000; operational outcomes are not dated.
- Attribution: Turkish public-institution action; direct Ecevit or cabinet authorization is not established.
- Contrary/limit: the source describes institutional purpose, not realized coverage, reconstruction completion, or distributional outcomes.
- Links: 6B.2, 6B.6, 6B.9.
- Source: [DASK TCIP overview](https://www.dask.gov.tr/en/about-the-tcip)

## Manifest operations

Apply these changes to `research-ledger-manifest.json`:

- Add E-151, E-152, E-153, E-154, E-155, E-156, and E-157 as new ledger items.
- Preserve E-143 and E-144, but replace their generic body locators with the precise locators above.
- Preserve E-146–E-149, but update their IMF locators to the paragraph/line ranges above and split E-146–E-149 where materially distinct claims remain bundled.
- Mark E-145 and E-150 as `context_only` / `non_attributable`.
- Mark E-151 and E-152 as `state_level_attribution_only`.
- Mark E-156 as `context_only` for personal integrity unless separately supported by a direct Ecevit asset, benefit, or decision record.
- No additional candidate was rejected in this pass.

The remaining gaps are not closed: no direct Ecevit signature, cabinet minute, personal asset disclosure, or nuclear command decision was located; no precise 2000 FAS/SIPRI nuclear-inventory record was found; and most TCIP and social-policy evidence remains collective-government or institutional rather than personal-ruler evidence.
